agentCan: Implement the full flow including the POST-callback handling
Design token storage for non-expiring credentials (vaulting, leak response)

approval.trigger: No review is documented. The Copper developer documentation read (Overview, Quickstart, Flow) describes no app review, no approval step, no private/public app distinction, and no pre-approval user or install cap. Once an application is registered, the documented flow works for any Copper user who authorizes it. The docs also describe no listing or marketplace submission process, timeline, or cost for OAuth apps. (Whether Copper runs any informal partner vetting outside these docs is unverified.)

blockers.detail: Unlike standard OAuth implementations where the code returns in a GET query string, Copper delivers the code in the BODY of a POST to your redirect_uri (the request body contains code on success or error on denial). Frameworks and endpoints that only handle GET callbacks will fail; the docs list an HTTPS POST-capable callback as a prerequisite in both the Quickstart and the Flow doc.
blockers.howToClear: Build the callback as an HTTPS endpoint that reads form-encoded POST bodies from day one.
blockers.title: The POST callback trap

blockers.detail: 'Currently, access tokens do not expire and do not need to be refreshed.' No refresh logic to build, but a leaked token is a standing credential: the documented flow includes no expiry safety net, and the token response carries no refresh_token.
blockers.howToClear: Vault tokens, monitor for misuse, and plan a disconnect story yourself; the docs document no revoke endpoint.
blockers.title: Non-expiring tokens cut both ways

blockers.detail: The scope parameter 'Must be developer/v1/all'. There are no granular or read-only scopes to request: authorization is full Developer API access for that user, or nothing.
blockers.howToClear: No clearance exists; design consent copy around full access.
blockers.title: Single all-or-nothing scope

sources.label: Overview: Authentication (API keys vs OAuth2.0 positioning)

tested: Read-only verification: the flow, scope, callback mechanics, and token behavior were checked against the three current developer.copper.com OAuth pages (no application registered, nothing submitted). The docs are minimal: two short pages are the entire documented OAuth surface.
unverified: The in-app registration process itself: where in Copper you create the OAuth app, what fields it requires, and who (any user vs. admin) may register one. The developer docs only state registration as a prerequisite that yields client_id/client_secret.
Whether Copper requires any partner agreement, review, or approval before other companies' users can authorize an app in practice (the docs describe none).
Any marketplace/integration-directory listing process, timeline, or cost.
Authorization code lifetime; PKCE support (not mentioned); whether state is echoed back on the POST callback.
Token revocation: no revoke endpoint is documented, and the docs read do not describe how a user disconnects an OAuth app.
Whether the token endpoint accepts the client_secret via HTTP Basic auth as an alternative to form body (docs show form-encoded body only).
API rate limits for OAuth-obtained tokens (not covered in the OAuth pages read).

alternatives: API keys (per-user tokens sent as headers X-PW-AccessToken, X-PW-Application: developer_api, X-PW-UserEmail; generated under System settings > API Keys; suitable for individual users / your own account only, with no per-customer consent flow)
flavor.recommended: A registered application using the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Grant with a confidential (server-side) client
flavor.why: Copper's Overview states the positioning directly: 'API Keys are suitable for individual users, while OAuth2.0 is the preferred approach for partner integrations', and the flow doc says the Authorization Code Grant is 'particularly well-suited for integrations that cater to existing Copper customers'. Registration yields a client_id and client_secret. There is only one documented scope and one documented grant type.

humanMust: Register the application and obtain the client_id and client_secret (the developer docs treat this as a prerequisite and do not walk through the registration UI)
name: Copper
nuances: Parameters must be form-encoded (application/x-www-form-urlencoded), 'similar to how they would appear in an HTML <form> element', for both the authorize request and the token request.
The documented token response is { access_token, token_type: Bearer, scope: 'developer/v1/all' }: no expires_in and no refresh_token.
The consent screen displays your app's name and requested permissions; the user clicks Authorize or Deny, and login is skipped if the user is already logged in.
Docs are minimal overall, so several production questions (registration UI, revocation, PKCE, code lifetime) have no documented answer; budget empirical verification time.
prerequisites: An HTTPS callback endpoint redirect_uri capable of receiving POST requests (a hard documented prerequisite)

steps.detail: Both the Quickstart and Flow docs treat this purely as a prerequisite ('You have registered your application and received your client_id and client_secret credentials'); the developer docs read do not walk through the in-app registration UI.
steps.title: Register your application

steps.detail: A hard documented prerequisite: the callback arrives as a POST, not a GET, with form-encoded parameters.
steps.title: Provide an HTTPS POST-capable callback endpoint

steps.detail: GET app.copper.com/oauth/authorize with form-encoded parameters: response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, scope=developer/v1/all (mandatory value), and optional state ('Any user-defined metadata to forward to the callback'). The user logs in (skipped if already logged in), sees your app's name and requested permissions, and clicks Authorize or Deny.
steps.title: Send the user to authorize

steps.detail: Copper redirects to your redirect_uri via a POST request; the request body contains code on success or error on denial/failure.
steps.title: Receive the code (by POST)

steps.detail: POST app.copper.com/oauth/token form-encoded with grant_type=authorization_code, code, redirect_uri, client_id, client_secret. Response: access_token, token_type Bearer, scope developer/v1/all, with no expires_in and no refresh_token: 'Currently, access tokens do not expire and do not need to be refreshed.' Call the Developer API at api.copper.com/developer_api/v1/... with Authorization: Bearer.
steps.title: Exchange the code; call the API

tagline: No documented review and tokens that never expire, but the thinnest docs of any CRM here: one mandatory all-or-nothing scope, and an authorization code that arrives in the body of a POST to your callback, which breaks standard OAuth libraries' assumptions.

time.active: ~1 hr of flow code (registration process itself is not documented)
time.total: Same day per the documented flow; no review documented
